idiom_name: bool + named predicate (#[must_use] fn is_empty(&self) -> bool)
implementation_notes: bool is a primitive with exactly two values, if/while conditions require it, arithmetic on it is a type error, and there are no implicit conversions (`true as i32` is an explicit cast), so the classic hazard cannot occur. The realization is a predicate method returning bool (`fn is_empty(&self) -> bool`), usually marked #[must_use] so a discarded result warns; when two boolean predicates must not be confused, wrap the flag in a newtype (`struct IsEmpty(bool)`) so a bare `if flag` is impossible and the call site must destructure the nominal type.
pitfalls: Casting is explicit but still possible (`flag as u8`); the type system stops accidental mixing, not deliberate conversion.
A predicate without #[must_use] can be called and discarded (`q.is_empty();`), so the attribute is what keeps the result from being silently dropped.
bool has no unknown state: if the question can also be unanswered, model it as Option<bool> or a state enum instead of forcing false.
`flag == true` is legal but unidiomatic and flagged by clippy::bool_comparison; use the value directly.
